extracted.intended_audience: participants in FCC proceedings (applicants, licensees, attorneys, commenters, petitioners, and Commission staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements governing ex parte presentations, sunshine-period restrictions, exemptions, filing/notice requirements, and related fee/challenge procedures in FCC proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver requests — fees returned if granted
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted fees, interest, or penalties will be returned if a waiver is granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests that do not include the required fees, interest, or penalties or forms will be dismissed unless a request to defer payment due to financial hardship, supported by documentation of the financial hardship, is included in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for reduction — payment and FCC Form 159 required
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for reduction of a fee, interest, or penalty must be accompanied by the full fee, interest, or penalty payment and FCC Form 159.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for reduction that do not include the required fees, interest, or penalties or forms will be dismissed unless a request to defer payment due to financial hardship, supported by documentation of the financial hardship, is included in the filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial-hardship waiver cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for waiver of a fee, interest, or penalty based on financial hardship, including bankruptcy, will not be granted to the extent the total regulatory and application fees, interest, or penalties for which waiver is sought exceeds $500,000 in any fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In computing this amount, the amounts owed by an entity and its subsidiaries and other affiliated entities will be aggregated. In cases where claim of financial hardship is not based on bankruptcy, waiver, partial waiver, or deferral above the $500,000 cap may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenges to fee determinations — written and proof required
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenges to determinations or an insufficient regulatory fee payment or delinquent fees should be made in writing and must be accompanied by suitable proof that the fee had been paid or waived (deferred), or by the required regulatory payment and any assessed penalty payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges submitted with a fee payment must be submitted to the address stated on the invoice or billing statement. Challenges not accompanied by a fee payment should be filed with the Commission's Secretary and clearly marked to the attention of the Managing Director or emailed to ARINQUIRIES@fcc.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration/appellate filings do not stay payment obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a petition for reconsideration or an application for review of a fee determination will not relieve licensees from the requirement that full and proper payment of the underlying fee payment be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for reconsideration and applications for review submitted with a fee payment must be submitted to the same location as the original fee payment. Failure to submit the fee by the date required will result in the assessment of a 25 percent penalty. If the fee payment should fail while the Commission is considering the matter, the petition for reconsideration or application for review will be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication directed to the merits or outcome of a proceeding, including any attachments to a written communication or documents shown in connection with an oral presentation directed to the merits or outcome of a proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded: communications inadvertently or casually made; inquiries concerning compliance with procedural requirements if the procedural matter is not an area of controversy; statements by decisionmakers limited to providing publicly available information; inquiries relating solely to status (unless they state or imply a view as to merits/outcome, timing, or preference). A status inquiry expressing concern about administrative delay is permissible so long as no view is expressed as to merits or a date by which the proceeding should be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Ex parte presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any presentation which (1) if written, is not served on the parties to the proceeding; or (2) if oral, is made without advance notice to the parties and without opportunity for them to be present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition applies irrespective of format (includes electronic text forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Decision-making personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Any member, officer, or employee of the Commission, or in the case of a Joint Board, its members or their staffs, who is or may reasonably be expected to be involved in formulating a decision, rule, or order in a proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes persons made a party or excluded from decisional process (e.g., separate trial staff). Unseparated Bureau or Office staff and Commission staff serving as case manager in a hearing proceeding are considered decision-making personnel with respect to decisions in which their Bureau/Office participates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Party (who becomes a party)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons who file an application, waiver request, petition, motion, request for declaratory ruling, or other filing seeking affirmative relief, and other specified categories (complainants served on subject, subjects of orders to show cause, persons given formal party status in hearings, and in certain rulemaking contexts, members of the public after an NPRM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual listeners/viewers submitting comments on a pending broadcast application generally will not become parties simply by service of comments. To be deemed a party for this subpart, a person must make the relevant filing with the Secretary, the relevant Bureau/Office, or the Commission as a whole. Being deemed a party for ex parte rules does not determine whether the person has satisfied other legal/procedural requirements or rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunshine period prohibition — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All presentations to decisionmakers concerning matters listed on a Sunshine Agenda, whether ex parte or not, are prohibited during the Sunshine period unless an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include presentations exempt under §1.1204(a); presentations related to settlement negotiations that comply with ex parte restrictions; widely attended speeches/panels (subject to limits); presentations by members of Congress or federal agencies under specified conditions. Presentations of substantial significance in a permit-but-disclose proceeding by a member of Congress may require placing a summary in the record per §1.1206(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sunshine period timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sunshine period begins the day after release of a public notice that a matter has been placed on the Sunshine Agenda and ends when the Commission either releases the text of a decision/order, issues public notice that the matter has been deleted from the Agenda, or issues public notice that the matter has been returned to staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition does not apply to filing a written ex parte presentation or memorandum summarizing an oral ex parte made on the day before the Sunshine period begins, or a permitted reply thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt presentations — categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain presentations are exempt from prohibitions in restricted proceedings, disclosure requirements in permit-but-disclose proceedings, and Sunshine-period prohibitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exempt types include: presentations authorized by statute or rules (e.g., filing required forms); to/from General Counsel concerning judicial review; emergency communications where safety or substantial property loss is threatened (must be placed in record promptly if not otherwise submitted); military/foreign affairs/classified security information; communications to/from federal agencies with shared jurisdiction (subject to disclosure of new factual information if relied on); communications to/from DOJ or FTC in specified circumstances (with disclosure of new factual information if relied on); discussions with advisory coordinating committees re frequency coordination; written presentations by non-parties (listeners/viewers) about certain broadcast applications; presentations made under confidentiality promises to protect individuals; and staff-requested presentations for clarification or settlement (with limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency coordination exemptions — disclosure of new factual information
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentations to or from another Federal agency or branch that involve matters over which both the agency and the Commission share jurisdiction are exempt provided any new factual information obtained through such a presentation that is relied on by the Commission will be disclosed by the Commission no later than the time of release of the Commission's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance coordination with the agency is required. If the agency does not wish disclosure, the Commission will not disclose or will disregard the information unless it fits another exemption. Disclosure of an agency's views does not preclude further discussions according to the exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff-requested presentations — service and disclosure limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentations requested by or made with advance approval of the Commission or staff for clarification or adduction of evidence, or for resolution of issues including possible settlement, are exempt subject to limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits include: (i) exemption does not apply to restricted proceedings designated for hearing; (ii) in restricted proceedings not designated for hearing, new written information or a summary of new oral information must promptly be served on other parties (service may be waived if burdensome, but copies then placed in record and public notice issued); (iii) in permit-but-disclose proceedings, disclosure of new written/oral information must follow §1.1206(b) (with Commission discretion to dispense with disclosure if it would interfere with investigation); (iv) if presentation is in a Sunshine-subject proceeding, disclosure must be per §1.1206(b) or other adequate notice; (v) if new information regarding merits is disclosed during settlement and Commission intends disclosure, Commission may defer disclosure until comment sought or settlement discussions terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt proceedings — list
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain proceedings are 'exempt' in which ex parte presentations may be made freely and need not be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exempt proceedings include: a notice of inquiry; petitions for rulemaking (except petitions requesting broadcast channel allotment); certain tariff proceedings prior to being set for investigation; proceedings relating to prescription of common carrier depreciation rates prior to public notice of specific proposed rates; and certain informal complaint proceedings under specified statutes. Note: petitions for rulemaking seeking preemption of state/local authority must be served on affected state/local bodies or will be dismissed as defective pleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit-but-disclose proceedings — designation
rubrics_metrics.description: In specified proceedings, ex parte presentations are permissible but must be disclosed pursuant to §1.1206(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These proceedings include (among others): informal rulemaking under section 553 after release of an NPRM (except broadcast channel allotment), rule changes adopted without an NPRM upon release of the order, declaratory rulings, tariff proceedings set for investigation, certain section 214 proceedings (unless designated for hearing), cable landing act license applications (unless designated for hearing), FOIA information-request proceedings, Joint Board proceedings, various section 220(b) depreciation proceedings upon public notice, proceedings to prescribe rate of return under section 205, applications for space and earth station authorizations, and petitions for Commission preemption under certain statutory provisions. If a permit-but-disclose proceeding involves only one 'party', that party and the Commission may freely make presentations to each other without the disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral ex parte disclosure requirement (memorandum)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who makes an oral ex parte presentation subject to this section shall submit to the Commission's Secretary a memorandum that lists all persons attending or otherwise participating in the meeting, and summarizes all data presented and arguments made during the oral ex parte presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memoranda must contain a summary of the substance and not merely a listing of subjects. More than a one or two sentence description of the views and arguments presented is generally required. If the oral presentation consisted in whole or part of data or arguments already in the presenter's written comments or filings, the presenter may provide citations to those prior filings (specifying relevant page/paragraph numbers) in lieu of summarizing them in the memorandum. For widely attended meetings, a transcript or recording may be filed as an alternative; staff may file a multiparty summary in its discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written ex parte presentations — identification and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: A written ex parte presentation and a memorandum summarizing an oral ex parte presentation (and cover letter, if any) shall clearly identify the proceeding to which it relates, including the docket number, and must be labeled as an ex parte presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents shown or given to Commission staff during ex parte meetings are deemed to be written ex parte presentations and must be filed consistent with this section. Additional copies of written ex parte presentations and notices of oral presentations, and any replies, shall be mailed, e-mailed or transmitted by facsimile to the Commissioners or Commission employees who attended or otherwise participated in the presentation, consistent with §1.49(a) and (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing formats and hardship exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings governed by §1.49(f) or where the Commission has an electronic filing method, written ex parte presentations and memoranda summarizing oral ex parte presentations and all attachments shall, when feasible, be filed through the electronic comment filing system in a native format (e.g., .doc, .xml, .ppt, searchable .pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If electronic filing would present an undue hardship, the person filing must request an exemption from the electronic filing requirement, stating clearly the nature of the hardship, and submitting an original and one copy of the written ex parte presentation or memorandum to the Secretary, with a copy by mail or email to the Commissioners or Commission employees who attended or participated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential information — request and redaction procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a filer believes that one or more documents or portions thereof should be withheld from public inspection, the filer should file electronically a request that the information not be routinely made available for public inspection pursuant to §0.459.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accompanying such a request, the filer shall include in paper form a copy of the documents containing the confidential information, and also shall file electronically a copy with the confidential information redacted. The redacted document shall be machine-readable whenever technically possible. Where the document contains metadata that is confidential or privileged, the filer may remove such metadata before filing electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines outside Sunshine period
rubrics_metrics.description: All written ex parte presentations and all summaries of oral ex parte presentations must be filed no later than two business days after the presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'business day' does not include a holiday and for computing time limits includes the full calendar day (12:00 a.m. ET to 11:59:59 p.m. ET). Examples illustrate how to compute the second business day depending on when the presentation occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines for presentations on day Sunshine notice released
rubrics_metrics.description: For presentations made on the day the Sunshine notice is released, any required written ex parte presentation or memorandum must be submitted no later than the end of the next business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written replies, if any, shall be filed no later than two business days following the presentation and must be limited in scope to the specific issues and information presented in the ex parte filing to which they respond. Example scenarios explain timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadlines during the Sunshine period (exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ex parte presentation is made pursuant to an exception to the Sunshine period prohibition, the required written ex parte presentation or memorandum summarizing an oral ex parte presentation must be submitted by the end of the same business day on which the presentation was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The memorandum shall identify on the first page the specific exemption in §1.1203(a) on which the presenter relies, and shall state the date and time of any oral presentation. Written replies to permissible ex parte presentations made pursuant to a Sunshine exception must be filed no later than the next business day and be limited in scope to issues and information presented. Examples illustrate the timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of incomplete or inaccurate ex parte notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of an oral ex parte presentation is incomplete or inaccurate, staff may request the filer to correct any inaccuracies or missing information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff may request corrections; filer must supply accurate/completed information as directed.
